quizQuestions.prompt: Who was the barren woman who prayed for a son and later dedicated him to the Lord?
quizQuestions.explanation: Hannah prayed earnestly for a child and dedicated Samuel to serve the Lord.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who was the old priest that young Samuel served and grew up under at Shiloh?
quizQuestions.explanation: Samuel served under Eli, the priest at the tabernacle in Shiloh.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did young Samuel do when he first heard the Lord calling his name at night?
quizQuestions.explanation: Samuel initially thought Eli was calling him, until Eli realized it was the Lord and told him how to respond.

options.text: He ran to Eli, thinking Eli had called him
He answered immediately, knowing it was God

quizQuestions.prompt: What sacred object did the Philistines capture in battle, causing their idol Dagon to fall before it?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Philistines captured the Ark of the Covenant, and Dagon's statue fell face down before it.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why did the elders of Israel demand that Samuel give them a king?
quizQuestions.explanation: Samuel's sons were corrupt judges, so the elders asked for a king to lead them like other nations.

quizQuestions.prompt: Where was Saul found hiding when Samuel searched for him to present him as king?
quizQuestions.explanation: Saul was found hiding among the baggage, reluctant to be made king.

quizQuestions.prompt: What disobedience of Saul's led Samuel to declare that God had rejected him as king?
quizQuestions.explanation: Saul disobeyed God's command to destroy all the Amalekites' plunder, sparing King Agag and the best animals.

options.text: He spared King Agag and the best plunder
He refused to fight the Philistines

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Samuel say to explain why God chose David over his older, more impressive brothers?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The LORD looketh on the heart," while man looks on outward appearance.

quizQuestions.prompt: About how tall was Goliath, according to 1 Samuel 17?
quizQuestions.explanation: Goliath's height is given as "six cubits and a span," roughly nine and a half feet.

options.text: About nine and a half feet

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David choose instead of Saul's armor before facing Goliath?
quizQuestions.explanation: David refused Saul's heavy armor, choosing his staff, sling, and five smooth stones instead.

options.text: Five smooth stones and his sling

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jonathan give David as a sign of their covenant of friendship?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jonathan gave David his robe, armor, sword, bow, and belt.

options.text: His robe, armor, sword, and bow

quizQuestions.prompt: What did a jealous Saul throw at David while David played the harp for him?
quizQuestions.explanation: Saul hurled his javelin at David, trying to kill him.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David do to prove he could have killed Saul in a cave at En Gedi, but chose mercy instead?
quizQuestions.explanation: David secretly cut off a corner of Saul's robe rather than harming him.

options.text: He cut off a piece of Saul's robe

quizQuestions.prompt: Which wise woman did David marry after her foolish husband Nabal died?
quizQuestions.explanation: Abigail became David's wife after Nabal's death.

quizQuestions.prompt: Whose spirit did the medium of Endor bring up for Saul, at his request?
quizQuestions.explanation: The medium conjured up the spirit of Samuel, who pronounced doom on Saul.

quizQuestions.prompt: Where did Saul and his sons, including Jonathan, die in battle against the Philistines?
quizQuestions.explanation: Saul and his sons died on Mount Gilboa.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who killed the priests of Nob for helping David while he was fleeing Saul?
quizQuestions.explanation: Doeg the Edomite, at Saul's command, killed the priests of Nob.

quizQuestions.prompt: What items did the Philistines send back with the Ark of the Covenant as a guilt offering?
quizQuestions.explanation: They sent golden emerods (tumors) and golden mice as a guilt offering.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David take from Saul's camp a second time, to again prove he meant Saul no harm?
quizQuestions.explanation: David took Saul's spear and water jug while Saul and his men slept.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jonathan and David do together in the field to warn David of Saul's intentions?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jonathan used a signal with arrows shot for a boy to retrieve, warning David to flee.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David compose after learning of Saul and Jonathan's deaths?
quizQuestions.explanation: David wrote a lament, including the line "How are the mighty fallen."

quizQuestions.prompt: Where was David first anointed king, before he became king over all Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: David was anointed king over Judah at Hebron.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David do as the Ark of the Covenant was brought into Jerusalem?
quizQuestions.explanation: David danced before the Lord with all his might as the ark entered the city.

quizQuestions.prompt: When David wanted to build God a temple, what did the prophet Nathan promise him instead?
quizQuestions.explanation: God promised David an everlasting dynasty (the Davidic covenant) instead of letting him build the temple.

options.text: Victory over all his enemies immediately

quizQuestions.prompt: Whose husband did David arrange to have killed in battle after committing adultery with her?
quizQuestions.explanation: David had Uriah the Hittite, Bathsheba's husband, placed in the front lines to be killed.

quizQuestions.prompt: What story did the prophet Nathan tell David to confront him about his sin with Bathsheba?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nathan told a parable about a rich man who stole a poor man's only lamb.

options.text: A parable about a rich man stealing a poor man's lamb
A story about two lost sheep
A riddle about a lion and a lamb
A dream about a fallen tower

quizQuestions.prompt: Which of David's sons led a rebellion against him, forcing David to flee Jerusalem?
quizQuestions.explanation: Absalom rebelled against his father David.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did Absalom die during his rebellion against David?
quizQuestions.explanation: Absalom's hair caught in a tree as he rode, and Joab killed him there.

options.text: Caught by his hair in a tree, then killed by Joab

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David cry out upon hearing of Absalom's death?
quizQuestions.explanation: "O Absalom, my son, my son!" — David mourned deeply despite Absalom's rebellion.

quizQuestions.prompt: What action of David's, numbering the fighting men of Israel, brought a plague as judgment?
quizQuestions.explanation: David's census of Israel angered God, and a plague struck the land as judgment.

options.text: Building an altar to a foreign god

quizQuestions.prompt: Which crippled son of Jonathan did David show kindness to for his father's sake?
quizQuestions.explanation: David sought out Mephibosheth and restored his grandfather Saul's land to him.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who served as the commander of David's army for most of his reign?
quizQuestions.explanation: Joab commanded David's army through many campaigns.

quizQuestions.prompt: What was Mephibosheth's physical condition, mentioned throughout his story?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mephibosheth was lame in both feet, having been dropped as a child while fleeing news of Saul's death.

options.text: He was lame in both feet

quizQuestions.prompt: Once he was firmly established as king, what did David ask his officials about survivors of the previous royal family?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness?"

options.text: "Is there anyone left of Saul's house I can show kindness to?"

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David eventually do to make things right after Nathan confronted his sin?
quizQuestions.explanation: David confessed and repented, saying "I have sinned against the LORD."

options.text: He denied it and hid the truth

quizQuestions.prompt: Where did David purchase land to build an altar after his sinful census, later the site of Solomon's temple?
quizQuestions.explanation: David bought the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite to build an altar there.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which of David's sons tried to seize the throne before Solomon was crowned?
quizQuestions.explanation: Adonijah tried to make himself king while David was still alive.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which foreign queen visited Solomon to test his wisdom with hard questions?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Queen of Sheba traveled to see Solomon's wisdom and wealth for herself.

quizQuestions.prompt: About how many years did it take Solomon to build the Temple in Jerusalem?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Temple took about seven years to build.

quizQuestions.prompt: What eventually happened to Solomon's devotion to God because of his many foreign wives?
quizQuestions.explanation: His foreign wives turned his heart away to worship other gods in his old age.

options.text: His heart turned to other gods

quizQuestions.prompt: What foolish advice did Rehoboam follow that caused ten tribes to rebel against him?
quizQuestions.explanation: Rehoboam followed young advisors and threatened to be harsher than his father Solomon.

options.text: Advice from young men to rule more harshly

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jeroboam set up at Bethel and Dan to keep the northern tribes from worshiping in Jerusalem?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeroboam made two golden calves for Israel to worship instead.

quizQuestions.prompt: What fed the prophet Elijah at the brook Cherith during a drought?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ravens brought Elijah bread and meat morning and evening.

quizQuestions.prompt: What miracle did Elijah perform for the widow of Zarephath during the famine?
quizQuestions.explanation: Her jar of flour and jug of oil never ran out for the rest of the famine.

options.text: Her flour and oil never ran out

quizQuestions.prompt: What consumed the sacrifice, altar, and water on Mount Carmel to prove the LORD is God?
quizQuestions.explanation: Fire fell from heaven and consumed everything, even the water in the trench.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did God speak to Elijah at Mount Horeb after he fled from Jezebel?
quizQuestions.explanation: God spoke not in the wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still small voice.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did Elijah symbolically call Elisha to follow him as his successor?
quizQuestions.explanation: Elijah threw his mantle (cloak) over Elisha while he was plowing.

options.text: He threw his mantle over him

quizQuestions.prompt: What did King Ahab covet that led Jezebel to arrange Naboth's murder?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ahab wanted Naboth's vineyard, and Jezebel had Naboth falsely accused and killed to get it.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Solomon pray for at the Temple's dedication regarding foreigners who come to pray toward it?
quizQuestions.explanation: Solomon prayed that God would hear even a foreigner's prayer, so all peoples would know His name.

options.text: That God would hear foreigners' prayers too
That foreigners be kept out entirely
That Israel would conquer all nations
That the Temple be hidden from them

quizQuestions.prompt: What filled Solomon's Temple after the Ark of the Covenant was placed inside it?
quizQuestions.explanation: A cloud, representing the glory of the Lord, filled the Temple.

options.text: A cloud, the glory of the Lord

quizQuestions.prompt: Who was the wicked queen married to King Ahab that promoted Baal worship in Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jezebel, a Phoenician princess, aggressively promoted Baal worship as queen.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Elijah do to prove the widow of Zarephath's dead son could be revived?
quizQuestions.explanation: Elijah stretched himself over the boy three times and prayed, and the boy's life returned.

options.text: He stretched over the boy and prayed
He anointed the boy with oil
He carried the boy to the Temple
He commanded a raven to revive him

quizQuestions.prompt: How did the prophet Elijah leave the earth at the end of his life?
quizQuestions.explanation: Elijah was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, with a chariot and horses of fire.

options.text: Taken up in a whirlwind with a chariot of fire

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Elisha ask for from Elijah before Elijah was taken up to heaven?
quizQuestions.explanation: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit.

options.text: A double portion of his spirit
To go with him to heaven

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Elisha tell Naaman the Syrian commander to do to be healed of his leprosy?
quizQuestions.explanation: Elisha told him to dip in the Jordan River seven times.

options.text: Dip in the Jordan River seven times
Offer a sacrifice at the Temple
Wash with oil from the Temple

quizQuestions.prompt: How did Elisha help a poor widow pay off her debts and save her sons from slavery?
quizQuestions.explanation: He multiplied her small jar of oil to fill many borrowed vessels, which she sold.

options.text: He multiplied her jar of oil
He gave her gold from the Temple
He found her a wealthy husband

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Elisha do for the Shunammite woman who had shown him hospitality?
quizQuestions.explanation: He raised her dead son back to life.

options.text: Raised her dead son to life
Gave her a house in Jerusalem

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to Elisha's servant Gehazi after he greedily and secretly took payment from Naaman?
quizQuestions.explanation: Gehazi was struck with the leprosy that had left Naaman.

options.text: He was made rich and blessed

quizQuestions.prompt: What lost tool did Elisha miraculously cause to float on the water?
quizQuestions.explanation: An iron axe head floated after Elisha threw a stick into the water.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which empire conquered the northern kingdom of Israel and carried its people away?
quizQuestions.explanation: Assyria conquered Israel and exiled its people.

quizQuestions.prompt: What sign did God give King Hezekiah to confirm he would recover from illness and live 15 more years?
quizQuestions.explanation: The shadow on the sundial moved backward ten steps as a sign.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did King Josiah do after hearing the words of the newly rediscovered Book of the Law?
quizQuestions.explanation: Josiah tore his clothes in distress and led Israel to renew their covenant with God.

options.text: He tore his clothes and renewed the covenant
He ignored it and continued as before

quizQuestions.prompt: Which empire eventually destroyed Jerusalem and the Temple, ending the kingdom of Judah?
quizQuestions.explanation: Babylon destroyed Jerusalem and the Temple, taking the people into exile.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened when a dead man's body touched Elisha's bones in his tomb?
quizQuestions.explanation: The man came back to life, even after Elisha's death.

options.text: The man came back to life

quizQuestions.prompt: What group of boys mocked Elisha for being bald, resulting in a tragic judgment?
quizQuestions.explanation: Youths from Bethel mocked him, and two bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of them.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did Elisha part the Jordan River after Elijah was taken to heaven?
quizQuestions.explanation: Elisha struck the water with Elijah's fallen mantle, and it parted just as it had for Elijah.

options.text: He struck it with Elijah's mantle
He prayed and it dried up overnight
He used the Ark of the Covenant
He built a bridge of stones

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Elisha do to help his servant see the invisible army of horses and chariots of fire protecting them?
quizQuestions.explanation: Elisha prayed that God would open his servant's eyes to see the spiritual reality.

options.text: He prayed for his servant's eyes to be opened
He gave his servant a vision through a dream
He anointed his servant's eyes with oil

quizQuestions.prompt: What does the book of 1 Chronicles begin with, tracing history from Adam?
quizQuestions.explanation: 1 Chronicles opens with lengthy genealogies starting from Adam.

quizQuestions.prompt: According to 1 Chronicles, who provoked David to take a census of Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: 1 Chronicles specifically says Satan provoked David to number Israel.

quizQuestions.prompt: Although David could not build the Temple himself, what did he do to prepare for it?
quizQuestions.explanation: David gathered vast materials and gave Solomon detailed instructions before his death.

options.text: He built a smaller version himself

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David organize the Levites to do for temple worship, according to 1 Chronicles?
quizQuestions.explanation: David organized the Levites into divisions for service, including musicians and singers.

options.text: Serve in organized divisions, including music

quizQuestions.prompt: Who died after touching the Ark of the Covenant to steady it during transport?
quizQuestions.explanation: Uzzah died after reaching out to steady the ark when the oxen stumbled.

quizQuestions.prompt: What charge did David give Solomon before he died, regarding the Temple?
quizQuestions.explanation: David charged Solomon to build the house of the Lord and to be strong and courageous.

quizQuestions.prompt: What group of skilled warriors is specifically listed and celebrated in 1 Chronicles 11-12?
quizQuestions.explanation: David's mighty men, celebrated for their courage and exploits, are listed in detail.

quizQuestions.prompt: How does the book of 1 Chronicles end?
quizQuestions.explanation: It ends with David's death and Solomon's enthronement as king.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David do with silver, gold, and other materials before his death, related to the Temple?
quizQuestions.explanation: David gave generously from his own treasury toward building the Temple.

options.text: He gave generously from his own treasury
He kept it all for his own use
He buried it for Solomon to find later

quizQuestions.prompt: What did David pray in thanksgiving as the people gave generously toward the Temple?
quizQuestions.explanation: David praised God, acknowledging that all riches come from Him: "all things come of thee."

quizQuestions.prompt: What filled the Temple when it was dedicated, so the priests could not continue ministering?
quizQuestions.explanation: The glory of the Lord, appearing as a cloud, filled the house.

options.text: The glory of the Lord, as a cloud

quizQuestions.prompt: What did King Jehoshaphat's army do before battle that led to victory without even fighting?
quizQuestions.explanation: Judah appointed singers to praise God as they marched out, and their enemies destroyed each other.

options.text: They sang praises before the army
They surrounded the enemy camp at night

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to King Uzziah after he presumptuously tried to burn incense in the Temple himself?
quizQuestions.explanation: He was struck with leprosy for overstepping the priests' role.

quizQuestions.prompt: What major spiritual reforms did King Hezekiah carry out early in his reign to turn Judah back to the LORD?
quizQuestions.explanation: Hezekiah reopened and cleansed the Temple and reinstated the Passover celebration.

options.text: Cleansing the Temple and restoring Passover

quizQuestions.prompt: What did the wicked King Manasseh do after being taken captive to Babylon in chains?
quizQuestions.explanation: Manasseh humbled himself and repented, and God restored him to his kingdom.

options.text: He escaped and continued his wickedness
He built a new pagan temple

quizQuestions.prompt: How does the book of 2 Chronicles end?
quizQuestions.explanation: It ends with King Cyrus of Persia's decree allowing the exiles to return and rebuild.

options.text: Cyrus's decree allowing the Jews to return

quizQuestions.prompt: What reforms did King Asa lead early in his reign?
quizQuestions.explanation: Asa removed idols and foreign altars, and called Judah back to God.

options.text: He removed idols and foreign altars

quizQuestions.prompt: What promise did God give Solomon about healing the land if His people humbled themselves and prayed?
quizQuestions.explanation: "If my people... shall humble themselves, and pray... I will hear from heaven and heal their land."

options.text: "I will hear from heaven and heal their land"
"I will destroy their enemies at once"

quizQuestions.prompt: Which queen mother seized the throne of Judah and tried to destroy the royal family, before being stopped?
quizQuestions.explanation: Athaliah usurped the throne and killed royal heirs, until the priest Jehoiada helped restore young Joash.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who helped rescue and crown young Joash as king after Athaliah's usurpation?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jehoiada the priest protected Joash and led his coronation.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Solomon request from God in a dream at Gibeon, at the start of 2 Chronicles?
quizQuestions.explanation: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern God's people well.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did the prophetess Huldah warn King Josiah would happen to Judah, after a lost scroll of Scripture was discovered during Temple repairs?
quizQuestions.explanation: Huldah confirmed that the judgment written in the Book of the Law would come on Judah because of their unfaithfulness.

options.text: The judgment written in the Book of the Law would come upon Judah

quizQuestions.prompt: Which Persian king issued the decree allowing the Jewish exiles to return to Jerusalem?
quizQuestions.explanation: King Cyrus of Persia issued the decree in fulfillment of prophecy.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who led the first group of exiles back to Jerusalem and began rebuilding the altar?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zerubbabel led the first return and helped rebuild the altar and lay the Temple's foundation.

quizQuestions.prompt: What slowed down the rebuilding of the Temple for many years?
quizQuestions.explanation: Opposition and discouragement from surrounding peoples halted the work.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which two prophets encouraged the people to resume rebuilding the Temple?
quizQuestions.explanation: Haggai and Zechariah prophesied, urging the people to finish the work.

quizQuestions.prompt: What was finally completed and dedicated in Ezra 6, after years of delay?
quizQuestions.explanation: The rebuilt Temple was completed and dedicated with joy.

quizQuestions.prompt: What was Ezra's profession, described at the start of his ministry?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezra was a priest and skilled scribe in the Law of Moses.

quizQuestions.prompt: What issue among the returned exiles caused Ezra deep grief when he arrived in Jerusalem?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezra grieved over the Israelites intermarrying with pagan peoples, compromising their faith.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Ezra do publicly when he learned of the people's unfaithfulness?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezra tore his garments, fell to his knees, and prayed a prayer of confession.

options.text: He tore his clothes and prayed in confession
He ignored it and moved on

quizQuestions.prompt: Who was the Persian king that sent Ezra back to Jerusalem with royal support?
quizQuestions.explanation: King Artaxerxes sent Ezra with a letter granting him authority and provisions.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Ezra do before setting out on the journey to Jerusalem, instead of asking the king for soldiers?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezra proclaimed a fast, asking God for a safe journey rather than relying on royal protection.

options.text: He proclaimed a fast and prayed
He delayed the journey a year
He asked for a large army escort

quizQuestions.prompt: What was Nehemiah's job serving the Persian king before he returned to Jerusalem?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nehemiah served as cupbearer to King Artaxerxes.

quizQuestions.prompt: What news made Nehemiah weep and mourn, leading him to pray and fast for days?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nehemiah heard that Jerusalem's walls were broken down and its gates burned.

options.text: The Temple had been rebuilt wrongly

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Nehemiah ask King Artaxerxes for permission to do?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nehemiah asked to be sent to Jerusalem to rebuild its walls.

quizQuestions.prompt: About how many days did it take to rebuild Jerusalem's wall, despite fierce opposition?
quizQuestions.explanation: The wall was completed in just fifty-two days.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which two opponents mocked and tried to stop Nehemiah's wall-building project?
quizQuestions.explanation: Sanballat and Tobiah repeatedly mocked and threatened the builders.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did the builders work once threats of attack grew serious?
quizQuestions.explanation: They worked with a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other, staying ready to defend themselves.

options.text: With a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other
In full armor at all times
They stopped working until it was safe

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Ezra do publicly in Nehemiah 8 that caused the people to weep and then celebrate?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezra read the Book of the Law aloud to the assembled people.

options.text: Read the Book of the Law aloud

quizQuestions.prompt: What did the Israelites do after hearing the Law read, according to Nehemiah 9-10?
quizQuestions.explanation: They confessed their sins and renewed their covenant with God in writing.

options.text: Confessed their sins and renewed the covenant
Demanded a new law be written

quizQuestions.prompt: What day did Nehemiah later enforce Israel to keep holy, after finding merchants working on it?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nehemiah enforced Sabbath observance, shutting the gates to keep out traders.

quizQuestions.prompt: What request did Nehemiah make of the king that revealed his sadness before explaining the reason?
quizQuestions.explanation: The king noticed Nehemiah's sad face, which was unusual, before Nehemiah explained about Jerusalem.

options.text: The king noticed his sad face
Nehemiah wrote a formal letter first

quizQuestions.prompt: How did Nehemiah organize the people to help build the wall faster?
quizQuestions.explanation: He assigned different families and groups each a specific section of the wall to repair.

options.text: Assigned each family a section of wall
Waited for the king's army to build it

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Nehemiah do when he discovered wealthy Jews charging unfair interest to their poorer countrymen?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nehemiah confronted them and required them to stop and return what they had taken.

options.text: He confronted them and made them stop
He ignored it as a private matter
He reported them to the Persian king

quizQuestions.prompt: What was Esther's original Hebrew name, before she became queen?
quizQuestions.explanation: Esther's Hebrew name was Hadassah.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why was Queen Vashti removed from her royal position at the start of Esther?
quizQuestions.explanation: Vashti refused to appear before King Ahasuerus and his guests when summoned.

options.text: She refused to appear before the king
She was caught plotting against him

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Mordecai instruct Esther not to reveal when she entered the king's palace?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mordecai told her not to reveal her Jewish identity or family background.

quizQuestions.prompt: What plot did Mordecai uncover and report, which was later recorded in the king's chronicles?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mordecai discovered a plot by two officials to assassinate the king.

options.text: A plot to assassinate the king
A plan to attack the Jews early
A scheme to rob the treasury

quizQuestions.prompt: Why did Haman become enraged and plot to destroy all the Jews in the empire?
quizQuestions.explanation: Haman was furious that Mordecai refused to bow down to him.

options.text: Mordecai would not bow to him

quizQuestions.prompt: What famous words did Mordecai say to persuade Esther to approach the king on the Jews' behalf?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?"

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Esther ask all the Jews in Susa to do before she approached the king uninvited?
quizQuestions.explanation: She asked them to fast for three days along with her and her maids.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Haman build for Mordecai, intending to have him executed on it?
quizQuestions.explanation: Haman built gallows, but was ultimately hanged on them himself.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did the king unexpectedly honor Mordecai instead of Haman, before Esther's banquet?
quizQuestions.explanation: Haman was forced to lead Mordecai through the city on the king's horse, proclaiming his honor.

options.text: Haman had to parade him through the city
He was given Haman's estate immediately
He was made prime minister on the spot

quizQuestions.prompt: What Jewish festival was established to commemorate the deliverance recorded in Esther?
quizQuestions.explanation: The festival of Purim commemorates the Jews' deliverance from Haman's plot.

quizQuestions.prompt: At the end of the book, what position did Mordecai rise to in the Persian kingdom?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mordecai became second in rank to King Ahasuerus, taking Haman's former position.

options.text: Second in rank to the king

quizQuestions.prompt: How was Esther chosen to become queen, replacing Vashti?
quizQuestions.explanation: She was brought into a search among the young women of the kingdom, and the king favored her above all others.

options.text: The king favored her above all the candidates gathered

quizQuestions.prompt: What relation was Mordecai to Esther, according to the book?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mordecai was Esther's cousin, who raised her as his own daughter after her parents died.

quizQuestions.prompt: How much silver did Haman offer to have put into the king's treasury to fund the destruction of the Jews?
quizQuestions.explanation: Haman offered ten thousand talents of silver.

options.text: He offered no money at all

quizQuestions.prompt: What is notable about the book of Esther that many readers observe, unlike most other Old Testament books?
quizQuestions.explanation: The book of Esther never explicitly mentions God's name, though His providence is clearly at work throughout.

options.text: It never explicitly mentions God's name
It was written entirely in poetry
It takes place entirely in Israel
